I love this glaze. I used Minspar 200 instead of FFF feldspar, and
also left out the bentonite. This helps the shrinkage and
flaking/crawling problem.


    Yuliya Z
   3 months ago


Gorgeous





                                                                                    hi i am new to pottery and i really love this glaze. i made it and
                                                                      glaze fire it in a nearby studio, but the result came out failed
                                                                                         like this. what do you think the problem is? is the temperature
                                                                        or the material?



                                                                                              Heather L
                                                                                 3 years ago

                                                                  Cukcukk Pinholing like that might mean that the kiln is
                                                                               cooling too fast (usually pinholes are from off-gassing
                                                                                   at the end stage of firing, and if it's cooled too fast the
                                                                             glaze can't "heal" the surface).


                                                                                   Also, did you add cobalt carb to this? That result is
                                                                            very blue for this recipe. If you're using shared studio
                                                                                 materials I'd worry about contamination between
                                                                                 ingredients or mislabelling.



                                                                                      Tessa S
                                                                             2 years ago





                                                                                                                                I got a great result from this glaze but after a lemon test, the
                                                                      glaze has an "oil spot" look to it which doesn't wash off, does

that indicate some leaching occured? The lemon slice was
                                                                     not discolored in any way.



                                                                                        Tamara Desoer
                                                                                    2 years ago

                                                                       Tessa S -- Copper is particularly good at destabilizing
                                                                    a glaze, and there is a lot in this one, combined with
                                                                              lowish silica and alumina. For some reason it's worse in
                                                                    a bristol glaze. Some degradation has occurred here
                                                                                        for sure. Beautiful, but not durable.



                                                                                              Tessa S
                                                                                    2 years ago

                                                                   Tamara Desoer Thanks! I am just getting into making
                                                                            glazes and still learning about everything. I guess this
                                                                                                     will only be for decoration purposes!
